title: Does Mixing Model Outputs Beat Mixing Samples? Cross-Model vs. Within-Model Diversity

original_idea.body:
# Does Mixing Model Outputs Beat Mixing Samples? Cross-Model vs. Within-Model Diversity

**Problem:** Self-consistency draws K samples from ONE model; multi-model ensembles draw from many. Given the hivemind, it is unclear whether cross-model sampling yields more EFFECTIVE diversity than sampling one model at high temperature.

**Direction:** For a fixed compute budget of K generations, compare K samples from one model at high temperature vs one sample each from K distinct small open models, measuring achieved answer diversity and downstream task accuracy/calibration.

**Why it matters:** If the hivemind makes cross-model sampling barely better, the perceived robustness of multi-vendor ensembles is overstated.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind (arXiv:2510.22954); correlated errors (arXiv:2506.07962); self-consistency literature.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible practical finding about ensemble robustness but the catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Controlled head-to-head with public benchmark and inference; clear methodology a novice+mentor can run.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped two-arm comparison with well-defined diversity/accuracy metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models, externally doable, informs third-party redundancy practice.

low_compute.reasoning: Fixed K generations on small models; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Self-consistency vs ensembling compared in places; clean diversity-source head-to-head partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Ensemble vs self-consistency studied; explicit effective-diversity head-to-head partly open.
